nodes.description: A patent document titled "Real-time ad-hoc spam filtering of email" describing a multi-pass ad-hoc spam message filtering approach.

nodes.entity_id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach
nodes.description: A filtering approach that dynamically generates a temporary classifier during a first pass based on results of a previously applied message filter that sorts messages into folders, then uses the classifier in a second pass to retrospectively inspect messages for misclassification.
nodes.id: Multi-Pass Ad-Hoc Spam Message Filtering Approach

nodes.description: A message filter that assigns messages to different message folders and stores first classification data in a persistent store; it is automatically executed independent of a user action.<SEP>A message filter that previously sorts messages into a plurality of different message folders and is configured to store first classification data in a persistent store.
A multi-pass message filter configured to generate a classification model based on a first pass analysis and use it in a second pass to identify misclassified messages.
A model generated during the first pass analysis that resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory location and is used to score messages and identify misclassifications.
Classification data generated by the first message filter and stored in a persistent store.<SEP>Classification data stored in a persistent store by the first message filter.

Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter to train the filter; it resides exclusively in a non-persistent memory store at the client device and is deleted upon providing the display of information.<SEP>Classification data generated by the first pass of the multi-pass message filter, configured to reside exclusively in a non-persistent memory store.

A device configured to receive messages, assign them to different message folders using the first message filter, and communicate the messages over the network to the message folders.<SEP>A device comprising a transceiver to send and receive data over a network and a processor operative to perform message management actions including first and second pass analysis and purging the classification model.

A device that executes the multi-pass message filter, generates and stores second classification data in non-persistent memory, scores messages, identifies incorrectly sorted messages, and provides a display of information enabling a user to move messages.<SEP>A user's device on which the classification model is maintained in memory and on which the first and second passes of the multi-pass message filter may execute entirely.
A medium including data and instructions whose execution on a computing device provides for managing messages.
A classifier employed by the multi-pass message filter.
A plurality of different folders into which messages are sorted by the first message filter and to which misclassified messages can be moved.
An identification of sorted messages that might be misclassified, generated by the second pass and displayed to the user.
A memory-resident-only location where the classification model resides, not stored on disk or another persistent data store.
A storage location where the first message filter stores first classification data.<SEP>A persistent data store where the first message filter stores first classification data.
A component of the network device that sends and receives data over a network.
A component of the network device operative to perform actions including first and second pass analysis and purging the classification model.

A book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders; a message sender's address in the address book is one basis for generating second classification data.<SEP>An address book associated with a recipient that is associated with the message folders, used in analysis for generating the classification model.
A header of a message, including a subject and originating network address, read during the first pass and used in classification model generation.
The contents of a message read during the first pass and used in classification model generation.
Attachments within messages read during the first pass.
Information about the sender of a message read during the first pass.
An interface on the client device through which the multi-pass message filter is selectable for execution by a user.

A message filter executed in multiple passes on sorted messages; a first pass trains the filter by generating second classification data, and a second pass uses that data to score each message and identify messages sorted into incorrect message folders.
A folder to which messages are assigned; a message may be identified as stored into an incorrect message folder and moved to another message folder.
A communication item received in plurality, assigned to message folders, scored by the multi-pass message filter, and potentially moved between folders.
A communications network over which messages are communicated between the network device and the client device.
A memory store at the client device where the second classification data resides exclusively.
A person who can select the multi-pass message filter for execution through an interface and can move an identified message to another message folder.
An interface on the client device through which a user can select the multi-pass message filter for execution.
